newsitem.title: UK: Britain raises interest rate by 0.25 point.
newsitem.headline: Britain raises interest rate by 0.25 point.

text.p: The Bank of England said on Wednesday it raised Britain's minimum lending rate by a quarter-point to 6.0 percent.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said in a statement explaining the surprise rate increase that he was determined to keep a firm grip on inflation.
Clarke met Bank of England Governor Eddie George earlier on Wednesday to discuss economic prospects and monetary policy.

"We have delivered a combination of healthy growth and sustained low inflation unseen for a generation. I am determined to maintain a firm grip on inflation to sustain this well into the future," Clarke said.
